title: Composite unit transport for the canonical prescribed-resolution comparison
statement: Let A,B,C be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] with bounded below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Let F:A\to B and G:B\to C be additive left exact functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive] such that F sends injectives to G-acyclic objects [def-sp-composite-acyclicity]. Given X, an injective resolution I [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and n a natural number, put K=F(I), L its zero extension and e=canonicalResolutionDerivedIso F I [def-pc-canonical-resolution-derived-iso]. Then \iota_GF^{-1} b^{-1} H^n(RG(e)) = \epsilon_GK^{-1} H^n(\mu_GK^{-1}) \rho_GL^{-1} H^n(\eta_G(L)), with b the canonical Grothendieck abutment identification [lem-sp-grothendieck-edge-maps] and \iota_GF the resolution comparison [lem-sp-derived-well-defined]. This is the composite-unit identity for the specific canonical e; all factors and the left-to-right composition convention are expanded by the recorded Lean statement.

proof.text: Expand grothendieckSpectralObjectHBotTopIso into the inverse composition isomorphism followed by the GF single-object homology comparison. Apply the ordinary canonical homology identity to GF and cancel the prescribed GF resolution comparison.

Evaluate the composition isomorphism unit equation on the extended injective resolution. Naturality along the augmentation and cancellation of the invertible F unit give resolutionDerivedIso_comp, already proved in this module. The acyclicity assumption supplies the composition isomorphism.

Use naturality of the G unit on the F map/extension isomorphism. Degreewise the GF map/extension comparison is G of the F comparison followed by the G comparison, including the zero terms. Apply homology, use quotient-homology naturality, and cancel the extension-homology comparisons. The remaining factors are the inverse G comparison and the G unit asserted on the right. The argument includes n=0.

theorem resolution_composite_unit_transport
    {A : Type uA} [Category.{vA} A] [Abelian A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vA} A] {B : Type uB} [Category.{vB} B]
    [Abelian B] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vB} B] {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C]
    [Abelian C] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vC} C] [HasDerivedCategory A]
    [HasDerivedCategory B] [HasDerivedCategory C] (F : A ⥤ B) (G : B ⥤ C)
    [F.Additive] [G.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [PreservesFiniteLimits G]
    (hFG : (⟨F, G⟩ : GrothendieckComposablePair A B C).SendsInjectivesToAcyclics)
    (X : A) (I : InjectiveResolution X) (n : ℕ) :
      (I.isoRightDerivedObj (F ⋙ G) n).inv ≫
          (F.grothendieckSpectralObjectHBotTopIso G hFG n).inv.app X ≫
          (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor C n).map
            (G.rightDerivedFunctorPlus.map (canonicalResolutionDerivedIso F I).hom) =
        (((G.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj
          ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex)).extendHomologyIso
          ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat (rfl : (n : ℤ) = n)).inv ≫
        HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
          (((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex).mapExtendIso
            ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat G).inv (n : ℤ) ≫
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctorObjQIso
          (G.mapCochainComplexPlus.obj
            ⟨((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex).extend
              ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat, 0, inferInstance⟩) n).inv ≫
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor C n).map
          (G.rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit.app
            ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.quotient B).obj
              ⟨((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex).extend
                ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat, 0, inferInstance⟩))
